To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the LAAP TOF and SP-AMS can measure the mass of SOA coating on biomass-burning soots with high sensitivity and that the LAAP-TOF can measure the mass and composition of the biomass-burning sooting core.

the sensitivity of the SP-AMS's BC mass measurement to the SOA coating is due to the difference in beam width for potassium versus black carbon and the LAAPTOFs ability to measure the mass of organic material coating biomass-burning soots.
the LAAP TOF can be used to obtain quantitative mass measurements from realistic biomass-burned soot particles, while the SP-AMS's rBC sensitivity does not plateau as a function of SOA mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ability of two commercial laser ablation particle mass spectrometry systems (LAAPTOF and SP-AMS) to measure the mass of refractory black carbon and organic matter in biomass-burning particles.
the effect of SOA coatings on the real-time measurements of biomass-burning particles by two commercial particle mass spectrometric instruments, the SP-AMs and the LAAPTOFs.
the response of two particle mass spectrometer instruments to the evolution of biomass-burning particles in the atmosphere.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LAAP-TOF is more robust than the SP-AMS for the analysis of biomass-burning particles.
the SP-AMS is more suitable for measuring the mass of black carbon, while the LAAPTOFs are more suitable for the mass and composition of organic matter in the presence of rBC.
the LAAP-TOF can provide quantitative measurements of the composition of complex soot particles in the atmosphere, but the SP-AMS cannot.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the LAAP-TOF can be used to measure the mass and chemical composition of the coating on individual biomass-burning soots, while the SP-AMS can be used to quantify the total mass of rBC in a mixed aerosol.
both SP-AMS and LAAPTOF are capable of detecting and measuring rBC mass, but with different sensitivities and limitations.
the SP-AMS is sensitive to BC mass, but not to SOA mass, and that the LAAP-TOF is sensitive to both BC and SOA mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the response of particle mass spectrometric techniques to soot-particle mixing state and composition is highly sensitive to the specific instrument design and laser ablation conditions.
the SP-AMS and LAAPTOF are sensitive to the presence of rBC and that the mass of rBC measured is a function of the amount of coating material.
both the SP-AMS and LAAPTOF are sensitive to the organic coating thickness on rBC particles and that the LAAPPTOF can provide quantitative mass measurements of rBC with SOA coatings.
